narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the school has decided this risk is high enough that you are required to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. Most important was your record of zero past class failures. Although this sounds positive, students who passed typically also had no failures, so your situation did not provide the strong positive signal that many successful students carry. The second most influential factor was your clear desire to pursue higher education. This strongly pushes the prediction toward passing, as every student who expressed this goal in the data ultimately succeeded. However, its helpful effect was not enough to fully overcome other influences. The third key factor was your mother's education level, which is 5th to 9th grade. This is lower than the education level of mothers of most students who passed and therefore nudged the outcome slightly toward failing.

To improve, focus on turning your ambition for higher education into concrete daily study habits. Since you already receive family support and have good family relationships, consider asking your mother or guardian to help you create a structured revision plan. Reducing your 10 absences, which is well above the average of under 4 days among students who passed, would also significantly strengthen your position.
